narr: A low pressure system and attendant cold front worked its way through the Ohio Valley on August 21st and into West Virginia. An abundance of moisture was already in place ahead of the frontal passage, which allowed for showers and storms ahead of the front to dump heavy downpours across northeastern West Virginia. Strong to severe storms progressed east of the Ohio River by the afternoon of the 21st, resulting in a few downed trees in Jackson County and Nicholas County. The threat then transitioned over to flash flooding as heavy downpours prevailed. Localized high water issues arose on roadways in the state that evening into the early morning hours of August 22nd, with one instance of a bridge washing out.
ev: Portions of a bridge on Cabin Run Road were washed away due to high water.
High water was observed along Route 16 near Big Otter.
Near the town of Sutton, Herold Road was inundated with water for a brief period of time.
High water was observed over several roads in the Turtle Creek area, resulting in road closures. These included Lick Creek Road, Mud River Road, Sparse Creek Road, and Big Ugly Creek Road.
Several roadways were flooded within the town of Mansfield.
Multiple sections of Wilsonburg Road were under water near the town of Reynoldsville.
